items.title: Des « valeurs judéo-chrétiennes » au « péril vert » : anatomie d’une supercherie politico-religieuse
items.description: Pendant des siècles, l’accusation de « peuple déicide » a nourri l’antijudaïsme chrétien et contribué à la persécution des juifs. Le renversement de cette représentation occidentale s’est réalisé à travers l’émergence de deux concepts stratégiques : les « valeurs judéo-chrétiennes » et le « péril vert ». Le premier concept redéfinit les références identitaires de l’Occident, tandis que le second désigne un nouvel adversaire après la disparition du « péril rouge ». D’où vient l’expression « judéo-chrétienne » ? 1- L’expression valeurs « judéo-chrétienne » a pris une dimension politique aux États-Unis durant les années 1930 et 1940 lorsque des responsables juifs ont démarché des catholiques et des protestants les incitant à utiliser cette expression pour combattre l’antisémitisme et défendre une « identité nationale commune ». Pendant la guerre froide, cette mystification a servi, avec le poids des premiers lobbies juifs, à distinguer l’Occident du communisme athée. Son usage s’est ensuite renforcé dans les milieux conservateurs américains. Par la suite, l’activisme de différents cercles politico-religieux juifs a consisté à phagocyter le christianisme, à s'approprier ses références morales et religieuses, puis à isoler peu à peu les musulmans en les érigeant en figure de l'étranger menaçant. Le christianisme, une religion qui prêche la compassion, la justice et la solidarité envers les opprimés se trouve parfois enrôlée au service d'un projet politique sioniste qui classe les vies, les souffrances et les droits par ordre d'importance. La foi sert alors à légitimer le pouvoir, et les valeurs universelles s'effacent devant les alliances stratégiques. Les juifs, persécutés pendant des siècles en Europe, portent une mémoire qui impose de combattre l'antisémitisme. Mais cette mémoire perd de sa force universelle quand on s'en sert pour discréditer toute critique d’Israël pour sa politique criminelle ou pour rendre inaudible la souffrance d'un autre peuple qui subit un génocide à ciel ouvert. Dans le même temps, les musulmans sont de plus en plus souvent enfermés dans une identité collective suspecte. Sommés de se justifier, à tout bout de champ, associés à la violence et présentés comme étrangers aux valeurs universelles, ils subissent une stigmatisation qui tend à faire de la violence un attribut intrinsèque de l’islam. Le « péril vert » pour remplacer le communisme 2- Le deuxième coup de « génie », si l’on peut dire, du sionisme international a consisté à forger le concept de « péril vert ». La chute du communisme, à la fin des années 1980, a privé l'Occident de son grand adversaire idéologique, et la disparition de l'Union soviétique a brouillé les repères hérités de la guerre froide. En se présentant comme la citadelle de la démocratie au milieu des monarchies autoritaires du Moyen-Orient et comme l’avant-poste occidental face au fondamentalisme musulman, Israël a rapidement compris qu’il devait préserver sa valeur stratégique et opérationnelle. Pour cela, il lui fallait trouver un adversaire de substitution au « péril rouge » communiste. En 1992, Leon T. Hadar, analyste juif américain spécialiste de la politique étrangère des États-Unis, publie une analyse consacrée au « péril vert ». Son analyse met en lumière la recherche d’un nouvel adversaire idéologique et il monte en épingle la construction d’une menace islamiste globale dans le débat stratégique américain. Le 11 septembre 2001 a consolidé cette lecture en plaçant la lutte antiterroriste au cœur de la politique étrangère américaine. L'islam, l'islamisme et le djihadisme ont été confondus, et la suspicion s'est étendue à des populations entières. Présenter l'ensemble comme un choc des civilisations a permis de passer sous silence les intérêts matériels et les calculs géopolitiques. Désigner un ennemi commun facilitait aussi la mobilisation des opinions, et réduisait au silence ceux qui dénonçaient le prix payé par les peuples arabes et musulmans. Le musulman remplace le juif Aujourd’hui, dans certains discours politiques et médiatiques, particulièrement en vogue en France parmi les fascistes du Rassemblement National et les médias de Bolloré, le musulman occupe une place comparable à celle qu’occupait naguère le juif. Il est présenté comme un corps étranger, un ennemi de l’intérieur sur lequel les sociétés européennes projettent leurs peurs et leurs frustrations. Entre certains médias connus pour faire le lit de l’extrême droite et de faux politiciens comme le raciste Éric Zemmour , qui déverse sa haine des Maghrébins et des Africains en les qualifiant de « hordes de barbares », pour mieux vendre sa théorie fumeuse du grand remplacement, le débat public s’enlise dans les amalgames et la stigmatisation tandis qu’une rhétorique de haine contribue à banaliser le racisme. Certains responsables de la droite, qui s’éloigne de plus en plus des valeurs républicaines, ne sont pas en reste. Bruno Retailleau , candidat à la présidentielle – que les méchantes langues surnomment Le Nabot Léon de la Vendée- entend ainsi inscrire les racines judéo-chrétiennes de la France dans la Constitution, dans le cadre de sa campagne haineuse visant les musulmans de France. Une telle proposition soulève la question de la place accordée aux différentes composantes de l’histoire et de l’identité françaises. Sous la plume venimeuse des idéologues de la fachosphère et dans leurs discours haineux, une partie du débat public a été transformée en affrontement de civilisations. Le soutien à Israël y est érigé en preuve de fidélité aux valeurs occidentales, tandis que les musulmans sont relégués à la marge et que toute contestation est assimilée à une hostilité envers l’Occident lui-même. Ainsi des valeurs dites « judéo-chrétiennes » sont appliquées à la carte, et les droits humains dépendent du rapport de force et des alliances. Alors que la réponse sensée n'est pas d'opposer les musulmans aux juifs, ni l'islam au christianisme, mais d'exiger la même justice pour tous, sans privilège identitaire et sans hiérarchie entre les victimes. *Amar Belani est ancien ambassadeur d’Algérie L’article Des « valeurs judéo-chrétiennes » au « péril vert » : anatomie d’une supercherie politico-religieuse est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Affaire Amal Mekki | Quand l’origine d’une journaliste devient un sujet de controverse
items.description: Le témoignage de la journaliste tunisienne, Amal Mekki, ancienne responsable de la rédaction arabophone de Swissinfo, met en lumière les tensions qu’elle dit avoir subies au sein du média suisse. Son identité arabo-musulmane, sa couverture de Gaza et la place de ses convictions personnelles sont au cœur du dossier. Djamal Guettala Le 30 octobre 2024, une question adressée à Amal Mekki par son supérieur hiérarchique allait prendre une place centrale dans le conflit professionnel qui l’opposait à la direction de Swissinfo . «Pouvons-nous mentionner que vous êtes juive ? », lui aurait écrit Mark Livingston, alors rédacteur en chef du média suisse, selon une enquête publiée le 16 octobre 2026 par Antithèse . Les auteurs, Martin Bernard et Sid Ahmed Hammouche, affirment avoir consulté ce courriel. La demande serait intervenue alors que Swissinfo préparait une réponse aux critiques de Daniel Rickenbacher, journaliste de la Neue Zürcher Zeitung (NZZ), sur le traitement du Proche-Orient par sa rédaction arabophone. Amal Mekki est tunisienne, arabe et musulmane. Dans son témoignage publié sur son site, elle confirme cet échange et raconte avoir rappelé à son supérieur son identité réelle, qu’il connaissait déjà. Pour elle, cet épisode marque le début d’une séquence au cours de laquelle ses origines et ses convictions auraient pris une place excessive dans l’appréciation de son travail. L’affaire pose une question qui dépasse le parcours individuel de cette journaliste : jusqu’où l’identité d’un journaliste et ses convictions personnelles peuvent-elles intervenir dans l’évaluation de son travail, notamment lorsqu’il couvre un conflit aussi sensible que celui de Gaza ? Des prises de position antérieures à son recrutement Le 2 décembre 2024, la NZZ publie un article consacré à Amal Mekki. Le journaliste s’appuie notamment sur d’anciennes publications de celle-ci sur les réseaux sociaux, ainsi que sur son travail autour du débat suisse relatif à une éventuelle interdiction du Hamas. Amal Mekki ne conteste pas l’authenticité de ces publications. Elle explique qu’elles étaient antérieures à son arrivée à Swissinfo et qu’elles exprimaient son soutien aux droits des Palestiniens. Elle conteste en revanche la manière dont ses responsabilités professionnelles et le travail de la rédaction arabophone auraient été présentés. Selon son témoignage, les quelques entretiens cités dans l’article ne représentaient qu’une partie de la couverture réalisée par Swissinfo sur la question du Hamas. Elle réfute également l’affirmation selon laquelle elle aurait été responsable de la majorité des reportages sur le Moyen-Orient. La distinction est importante. Les prises de position publiques d’un journaliste peuvent légitimement susciter des questions déontologiques. Mais leur existence ne suffit pas, à elle seule, à démontrer un manquement professionnel. Encore faut-il examiner les articles publiés, les méthodes de travail, les sources mobilisées et les règles appliquées par la rédaction. «À cause de qui vous êtes» Dans son récit, Amal Mekki situe un autre moment décisif au 6 décembre 2024, lors d’une réunion avec Mark Livingston et un responsable des ressources humaines. Elle explique qu’elle souhaitait obtenir des corrections concernant les informations qu’elle jugeait trompeuses et être protégée face aux conséquences de la controverse. Elle affirme que la discussion a rapidement porté sur son rapport entre engagement et journalisme. Elle rapporte surtout que son supérieur lui aurait demandé de prendre ses distances avec l’expression «occupation israélienne» , en invoquant, selon elle, «qui elle est» . La journaliste dit avoir contesté cette demande. À ses yeux, le terme employé renvoyait à la situation des territoires palestiniens occupés et ne pouvait être écarté au seul motif de son identité. Cet échange, tel qu’elle le rapporte, est au centre de son accusation : elle estime que son origine arabe et sa confession musulmane ont pesé dans la manière dont ses prises de position ont été appréciées. Il reste toutefois nécessaire de distinguer son interprétation des événements des intentions des personnes mises en cause. Les éléments disponibles ne permettent pas de trancher à eux seuls l’ensemble des responsabilités. Une affaire qui interroge les médias européens Amal Mekki indique ne pas être retournée travailler à Swissinfo après cette réunion. Selon son témoignage et l’enquête d’ Antithèse , son contrat a pris fin le 31 juillet 2026. Elle présente son expérience comme celle d’une journaliste dont les convictions et l’identité auraient fini par prendre le pas sur l’examen de son travail. Cette lecture est la sienne. Les accusations qu’elle formule ne doivent pas être présentées comme des faits judiciairement établis en l’absence d’une décision en ce sens. Pour autant, son témoignage soulève des questions légitimes sur la manière dont les rédactions gèrent les désaccords liés à la couverture du conflit israélo-palestinien. La neutralité journalistique ne signifie pas l’absence de convictions personnelles. Elle repose d’abord sur des méthodes : vérifier les faits, confronter les sources, distinguer les informations des commentaires et appliquer des règles professionnelles cohérentes. Ces exigences doivent être les mêmes pour tous. Elles ne sauraient dépendre de l’origine d’un journaliste, de sa religion ou de l’histoire personnelle qu’il porte avec lui. À l’inverse, toute accusation de discrimination doit pouvoir être examinée à partir d’éléments précis, sans présumer d’emblée de la culpabilité des personnes concernées. L’affaire Amal Mekki ne permet pas, à elle seule, de tirer une conclusion générale sur le traitement des journalistes arabes dans les médias européens. Elle met néanmoins en lumière une difficulté réelle : lorsque la guerre à Gaza entre dans les rédactions, les débats sur les mots, les angles et l’impartialité peuvent aussi devenir des débats sur l’identité de ceux qui les portent. Et si cette «règle» est appliquée aux journalistes arabo-musulmans, elle devrait l’être à tous les journalistes, dont l’accusateur de la journaliste tunisienne, Daniel Rickenbacher, historien, chercheur postdoctoral à l’Institut Ben Gourion d’études sur Israël et le sionisme, au Néguev, qui publie depuis des années dans des médias ouvertement proches d’Israël : Audiatur-Online, Fathom Journal, Jüdische Allgemeine . Les deux poids, deux mesures, encore et toujours… C’est précisément là que se joue l’enjeu professionnel. Une rédaction doit pouvoir questionner les choix éditoriaux de ses journalistes, mais elle doit aussi être en mesure d’expliquer ses décisions et de démontrer que les mêmes critères sont appliqués à tous. Dans cette affaire, les documents et témoignages rapportés par Antithèse et par Amal Mekki appellent un examen attentif, sans confondre les accusations formulées avec des conclusions déjà établies. items.title: Mali : valises de billets, kilos d’or, chaîne en diamant et voiture de luxe… Le mariage du fils du couple Diallo fait exploser les compteurs du faste !

items.title: Sanwo-Olu appoints Sanuth as new LAWMA MD
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has appointed Dr. Hassan Sanuth as the new Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), following reports that the incumbent, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin, had been asked to resign over persistent waste management challenges across the state. However, relevant state authorities had yet to officially confirm the development as of press time. Sources familiar with the matter said the governor had become dissatisfied with the continued accumulation of refuse on major roads, residential streets and drainage channels despite directives to improve waste collection. One of the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Sanwo-Olu had asked Gbadegesin to resign over the weekend, although the outgoing managing director was reportedly seeking more time to address the situation. “The directives aim at addressing the waste challenges in the state,” the source told Vanguard. Sanuth, before his reported appointment, was the Director of Sanitation Services in the Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources. The reported development comes amid renewed concerns over waste collection and disposal across Lagos, despite the state government’s recent interventions to address the problem. Sanwo-Olu Declares Emergency on Waste Management Recall that Sanwo-Olu, during a visit to the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota about a month ago, expressed dissatisfaction with the heaps of refuse across the state, describing the situation as “embarrassing”. The governor ordered immediate action, directed a comprehensive overhaul of LAWMA’s operational structures and management, and declared a state of emergency on waste management. Accompanied by his deputy, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, Sanwo-Olu met with stakeholders in the waste management sector at the dumpsite to assess the challenges affecting municipal waste collection and outline immediate, medium- and long-term solutions. He acknowledged the slow pace of waste collection, attributing the situation partly to the failure of Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators to meet their obligations in the preceding weeks. The governor also said waste compaction activities were ongoing at the Olusosun and Solous 3 dumpsites, adding that completing the exercise would facilitate faster evacuation. He explained that recent fire incidents at the dumpsites had slowed operations but said work had resumed, with contractors working to clear the sites for daily waste disposal. According to him, completing the projects would enable each dumpsite to receive about 450 trucks of municipal waste daily, effectively doubling the capacity of PSP operators. Refuse Accumulation Persists Across Communities Despite the interventions, residents have continued to report refuse accumulation in several parts of Lagos, including Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2. The situation has prompted repeated complaints about decomposing waste along streets, road medians, major highways and drainage channels. A source familiar with the matter said the governor was dissatisfied that the situation had not improved despite his earlier directives. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive,” the source said. The source added that Gbadegesin was reportedly appealing for more time and seeking the intervention of prominent individuals. In a weekly update on waste management posted on his X handle on Saturday, however, Gbadegesin reported progress in clearing some affected areas and sustaining collection services on selected routes. He said Mile 2 had been cleared, with routine collection sustained, while three additional trucks had been deployed to Doyin-Orile and its environs. READ ALSO: Lagos evacuates Ago Palace Way refuse bins after Vanguard report “11 of the 15 routes in this week’s programme now have field updates,” he wrote. According to the update, daily waste collection had been maintained on Ijesha Road and Itire-Ikate, while Bucknor-Ijegun had been cleared and placed on a three-times-weekly collection schedule. He also said Okeira and Oluodo had been placed under LAWMA’s interim service following the termination of their PSP arrangements, while collection continued at Ogolonto and Igbokusu. Obalende, he added, had been cleared, provided with a waste bin and placed under surveillance, while clearance operations continued at Iraye. Gbadegesin identified Apapa, Abesan Estate, Idimu-Ejigbo Road and the Isheri-Igando corridor as the four routes awaiting field updates. “The objective is to progress from clearance to sustained collection and prevention of recurrence, not simply remove visible waste,” he said. Gbadegesin was reappointed to head LAWMA by Sanwo-Olu following the governor’s re-election. Meet the Reported Successor Dr. Hassan A. Sanuth holds a PhD in Environmental Microbiology and a master’s degree in Microbiology from the University of Ibadan. His research interests include epidemiology, biodegradation and bioremediation, and environmental monitoring. He also holds certificates in Environmental Monitoring and Modelling from the Institute for Water Education in Delft, the Netherlands, and Multilevel Water Governance from The Hague Academy for Local Governance. Sanuth has more than 23 years of public service experience and has worked in various environmental management and protection departments, including pollution control, billing and monitoring, conservation, and ecology. He also served as Nigeria’s focal point for environment under the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation-sponsored Collaborative Action for Sustainable Tourism programme in sub-Saharan Africa. Sanuth is a member of the Science Association of Nigeria, Nigeria Environmental Society and American Society for Microbiology, as well as an associate of the Nigerian Institute of Management. items.title: Hindsight: Sekondi Sports Stadium reopens, but sustainability and functionality issues remain
items.description: On October 13, the Sekondi Sports Stadium came back to life. For the first time in seven years, the stadium hosted a competitive, elite-level football match: an Olympic Qualifier between Ghana’s Black Queens and Mauritius. In the end, the Queens put seven past Mauritius. A fitting result to mark the reopening of a stadium many had not used in nearly a decade. Much has changed since it was last used. The beams, weak compression rings, weak trusses, and corroded roofing sheets have all been replaced. Now, they spot an unmistakable coating system, ostensibly to prevent deterioration in the manner of the former state. The old plastic seats, previously covered in dust and whatever else its recent users left on it, have also been replaced by brightly-colored new ones that, From the West Stand, East through to the North Stand, every single seat has been removed and replaced. Approximately twenty-five feet from the stands, lies familiar, green-pigmented plants joined together by their stems and held in place by the soil – the playing surface. Before last week’s opening, the last memory fans had of the pitch was an insect-infested, brownish grass. Like crops on farms in the dry seasons, whose owners have relocated to the next village in search of water: nutrient-deficient and neglected. Now, however, it has a familiar green look to it, even if not entirely Bermuda, Kentucky, or Perennial grass. The scoreboard has been fixed too. But that is as far as it goes. They only fixed the broken parts without addressing the main challenges with the stadium. Concerns. The stadium is still is very limited in terms of what it can host. It can host track and field events, but the results recorded will not be recognized internationally because the stadium does not meet required standards. The tartan tracks, for example, are not internationally certified. So do not expect Benjamin Azamati or any of Ghana’s elite-level athletes to be running on it. What it can do is host inter-school events in the Sekondi Takoradi Metropolis like it always has – even then, there is a limit to the disciplines that can be held there. There is no space for basketball, volleyball, or tennis. Next year will be the 20th anniversary of the Sekondi Sports Stadium. For a renovation this close to the anniversary, it would have been prudent to consider fixing these issues once and for all. Maintenance and sustainability If anything symbolizes the poor maintenance culture at the stadium, it is the forty rooms that were marked as hotel spaces, but have not been touched since the stadium was opened in 2007. For nineteen years, the forty rooms have been empty. The NSA could have rented the rooms out as offices, but chose not to. The internal bureaucracies of the institution have often been blamed. But it is hard to take these seriously. After all, it is not as though the process for its lease was ever set in motion. Across seven different governments and a million appointees to its head office and the Sports Development Officers (NSA Regional Heads), nobody did anything about the quietly sleeping 40 rooms. Probably because the empty rooms did not speak loudly enough. Or if we pretended the media had not made enough noise to draw the NSA’s attention. At the moment, there are no plans to furnish the rooms and use them for the intended purposes.

items.title: World Cup visa scandal: $26,000 paid to police on behalf of Ampofo Ankrah
items.description: A total of $26,000 has reportedly been paid to the police on behalf of suspended National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, part of the $56,000 he is alleged to have received as commission from proceeds linked to the World Cup visa scandal . People familiar with the payment told JoySports that the money was paid last week by a friend of Mr Ankrah, with the approval of the suspended NSA boss and his lawyers. The sources said the individual had undertaken to pay the outstanding balance. JoySports contacted Mr Ankrah on 15 October to verify the payment, but he did not respond to the request for comment. The payment comes amid investigations into allegations of visa racketeering involving NSA officials and other individuals in connection with arrangements for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Mr Ankrah has denied the allegations levelled against him in a petition filed by the NSA’s former Chief Operations Officer, Yaw Gyamfi Kusi Awere. “I challenge any man or woman to come forward and say they have given me even a penny to help them to process visas. I have never and will never do such a thing,” he said in a statement last month. Earlier this month, his lawyer, Jerry Avenorgbor, told Newsfile that the police were investigating the allegations “aggressively” and that Mr Ankrah had made multiple appearances before the Criminal Investigations Department (CID). Sources familiar with the investigation said Mr Ankrah had told investigators that he and Mr Gyamfi had exchanged money over the course of their relationship, which dates back to 1989. However, he maintained that he did not know the money in question represented commission from prospective travellers seeking visa assistance. Mr Gyamfi filed the petition seeking police intervention to recover the $56,000 he alleged Mr Ankrah had received as commission from prospective travellers. Mr Ankrah maintains that the allegations against him concerning visa-related payments are unfounded. Sources familiar with this scheme said about 180 prospective travellers had paid between $4,000 and $25,000 for visa assistance in the hope of travelling to the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico. None of the applicants seeking support to travel to Canada received visas, while about 37 out of the 180 applicants obtained visas. A list of 90 people submitted by Mr Ankrah to the Sports Ministry on 19 May 2026, seeking support for visa applications, did not result in any of the applicants receiving a visa appointment date. Mr Gyamfi has claimed that the individuals paid money before their names were included on the list submitted for visa support. The people are demanding a refund. Mr Ankrah has denied knowledge of wrongdoing and recently told Sporty FM that he was “200 percent sure” he would “be exonerated”. JoySports investigation uncovered the use of an office at the NSA by Tribe Culture Fest to operate the visa-related scheme. The NSA has, however, said it did not authorise visa facilitation activities at its premises. On 1 October, President John Dramani Mahama suspended Mr Ankrah as Director-General of the NSA pending investigations into the alleged visa racketeering. The suspension followed a report submitted to the Presidency by Sports Minister Kofi Adams concerning the allegations. The police investigation is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged payments, the roles of the individuals involved and whether any offences were committed. Meanwhile, President has set up a committee a the Jubilee House Chaired by Professor Francis Dodoo to investigate the scandal.

items.title: ‘My message twisted’ - Obi denies telling UK-based Nigerians to abandon loved ones
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has denied asking Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to abandon relatives who depend on them for financial support, saying his message about hardship in Nigeria was distorted by political opponents. Obi said he appreciated Nigerians in the diaspora who made sacrifices to support their families at home, stressing that his concern was the country’s dependence on remittances to meet basic needs. In a statement titled “My Message Has Been Twisted”, posted on X on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said he never asked Nigerians abroad to stop supporting their loved ones. “I deeply appreciate Nigerians in the diaspora who work tirelessly and make enormous sacrifices to support their families back home,” he said. “Their remittances pay for school fees, hospital bills, rent, and feeding expenses. Their patriotism and sacrifices deserve our profound respect. I never asked them to abandon their loved ones.” Obi said his message was aimed at drawing attention to the economic conditions forcing millions of Nigerians to rely on relatives abroad for their survival. “My concern is that Nigeria should not remain a country where millions depend on relatives abroad for basic survival,” he said. “Our goal must be to build a nation that provides jobs, affordable healthcare, quality education, and economic opportunities for its citizens.” He accused political opponents of misrepresenting his comments, insisting that his position was about addressing the causes of hardship rather than discouraging financial assistance to families. “Political opponents may twist my message, but the truth remains clear: I am not asking Nigerians abroad to abandon their families. I am advocating for a Nigeria that will no longer abandon its own people,” he said. The clarification followed backlash over comments Obi made during a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. In a video that went viral, Obi urged Nigerians in the UK to stop giving money to relatives and others at home who asked them for financial assistance, arguing that such support could ease hardship without addressing its underlying causes. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” he said. Obi attributed the country’s economic difficulties to poor leadership and urged Nigerians abroad to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for leaders who would prioritise productivity and economic opportunities. items.title: Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to N4,000/$ — Oyedele
items.description: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to petrol subsidy could trigger capital flight, weaken investor confidence and push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning on Monday during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. He said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. The minister ruled out reversing the reforms, warning that even a signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration was considering reinstating petrol subsidy could unsettle financial markets, increase borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious,” he said. Oyedele warned that any indication of a possible return to subsidy would trigger an immediate market reaction. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. “Airfares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards 3,000, 3,500 or even 4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he stated. The minister added that capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also turn to the dollar as a hedge against uncertainty, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. Oyedele also rejected suggestions that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins amounted to a return to subsidy. He explained that the reduction was a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources, arguing that a company’s decision to lower its profit margin to make a product more affordable should not automatically be classified as a subsidy. items.title: Declared dead: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
items.description: Kamta Prasad has been shuttling between government offices in Delhi trying to prove he is not dead. The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India’s electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from “logical discrepancies” to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored. He has had to forgo his daily wage of 250 Indian rupees that supports his family of four to scurry around the city to reverse the error. “I panicked when I heard about it,” said Prasad, who is among 4.2 million Delhi voters struck off the list, according to the draft rolls published by the poll body on August 31. “Since then I’ve been going everywhere to prove that I’m alive.” Kamta Prasad, 53, a voter who is listed as “Kanta Prasad” and is declared dead in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list published on August 1, 2026, cleans his glasses at his workstation, in New Delhi, India on October 19, 2026. —Reuters The deletions have triggered a political storm, with opposition parties and youth groups staging near-daily protests in New Delhi and elsewhere, which have been met with force by the police. They allege Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the revision to benefit Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a charge denied by both the commission and the BJP. ‘Nobody listens’ According to Rajendra Kumar, a volunteer with non-profit Jan Sarokar, about 2,000 of the roughly 9,000 voters in Prasad’s block were struck off after the revision, classified as absent, shifted, deceased or registered elsewhere. Prasad is the only person in this block who has been declared dead but several similar cases have been reported by local media across the country. The Election Commission has said it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can file claims, submit supporting documents and pursue appeals before the rolls are finalised. For voters such as Prasad, however, exclusion leads to a bureaucratic maze, and depending on the circumstances they may have to provide proof of life, establish residency, correct alleged discrepancies or submit fresh documentation. That involves repeated visits to election offices, hearings before electoral officials and multiple rounds of appeals, with some spending weeks or months trying to restore their names. “I told them I voted in the last assembly and general elections and have been voting for 35 years, but nobody listens,” Prasad said. India’s Election Commission did not reply to a request for comment for this story. Register as a new voter Following weeks of protests, the Election Commission ordered fresh verification in some states, including Delhi, and Prasad said officials had assured him his name would be restored. Kamal Lal, a 38-year-old private school teacher in Delhi, was marked as “shifted” even though he still lives in a settlement beneath a flyover with dozens of other families. Kamal Lal, 38, a teacher and voter who says his name was removed from the voter list and is placed in the Permanently Shifted category in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list, stands below a flyover in New Delhi, India on October 16, 2026. —Reuters “It is very disappointing that we have been voting in this country and now our names have been cut because we do not have land papers or a water bill,” he said. Lal said he first learned of his exclusion in September and has since approached election officials, attended hearings and filed multiple reinstatement applications. For some excluded voters, the remedy offered by officials has brought little comfort: rather than restoring their previous registrations, they were advised to apply afresh as new voters. For poorer voters, fears run even deeper. Mamta, a voter whose name was removed from the voter list and put under the Permanently Shifted category in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list published on August 1, 2026, poses for a photograph during a Reuters interview at her house in New Delhi, India on October 15, 2026. —Reuters “Now local election officials are asking us to register as new voters, and my husband is strongly opposed to that because he has voted in the last few elections,” said 39-year-old Mamta, who does not use a surname. “I am worried that if our names are not restored to the list, I could lose access to subsidised ration and other government welfare schemes.” Header image: Kamta Prasad, 53, a voter who is listed as “Kanta Prasad” and is declared dead in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list published on August 1, 2026, walks through an alley in New Delhi, India on October 19, 2026. —Reuters

items.title: National grid crashes 81% to 675MW, as 9 plants go off
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s grid electricity supply crashed by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW, following a drop in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 2. The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid before the incident at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW. However, by 1pm, the number of plants on the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply plunged to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour. The plants that went offline included Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants. The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before experiencing the steep drop at 1pm. Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, representing an improvement of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak. In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge. The company said TCN’s technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that power supply was gradually being restored to its feeders. “We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits,” AEDC said, while apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption. Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced electricity supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of power allocated to it from the national grid. In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply. It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible. However, NISO said it had stabilised the national grid following multiple trippings on the 330-kilovolt (kV) transmission network. In a statement on Monday, the system operator said the incident occurred at approximately 12:40pm on October 19, 2026. It said it immediately implemented corrective measures in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations. According to NISO, restoration efforts had been successfully completed and the national grid had returned to normal operation. The operator clarified that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims. items.title: Health authorities dismiss reports of insulin shortage, cite unavailability of one brand
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Authorities on Tuesday denied reports of a widespread insulin shortage in the country, saying that only one brand was unavailable due to international supply constraints. The clarification came after reports of a shortage across Pakistan emerged on social media. The health ministry and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) maintained that alternatives for the unavailable brand remained available in the market. “Insulin glulisine (Apidra, Sanofi) is currently unavailable due to international supply constraints. Alternate rapid-acting analogues within the same pharmacological class, specifically insulin aspart (NovoRapid, Novo Nordisk) and insulin lispro (Humalog, Eli Lilly), are readily available nationwide,” ministry spokesperson Sajid Shah said. “All other primary insulin classes remain fully accessible across Pakistan,” he added. He explained that insulin analogues — one of the two categories of medically approved insulin — include rapid-acting, long-acting and premixed formulations. The other category, human insulin, includes short-acting and intermediate-acting formulations. The spokesperson added that patients who have been prescribed Apidra “should consult their attending healthcare provider prior to modifying their regimen”. “Any transition to an alternative insulin formulation requires precise dose titration and tailored monitoring to maintain optimal glycaemic control,” he said. In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients. According to the association, at least 80 important medicines were unavailable, with 25 having no substitutes. These drugs included life-saving medications for diabetes, cancer, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, heart disease and psychiatric disorders. In March 2026, PMA cautioned about the severe shortage of essential paediatric tuberculosis (TB) as well as cancer medications, warning that the humanitarian crisis was getting worse with each passing day, while calling for immediate intervention.

items.title: Customs reviews recruitment complaints, screens out 397 applicants
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has opened a fresh window for reviewing complaints from applicants disqualified during its recent recruitment exercise, following protests by some shortlisted candidates barred from proceeding to the training college. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, directed a case-by-case reassessment of the complaints after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. The NCS spokesperson, Abdullahi Maiwada, a Deputy Comptroller of Customs, disclosed this in a statement, saying the review was intended to ensure that legitimate grievances received appropriate attention. Adeniyi, however, warned that the exercise would not guarantee automatic admission, stressing that all affected candidates would undergo fresh screening and that anyone found to have engaged in certificate fraud or other criminal conduct would face prosecution. According to Maiwada, the recruitment process involves several stages of verification, including credential and document checks, physical fitness and endurance assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. He disclosed that 397 applicants were identified with issues relating to substance abuse, physical fitness, medical records, age and submitted documentation, while other candidates were disqualified over irregularities detected during the screening exercise. The spokesperson explained that appearing on the final shortlist did not automatically entitle an applicant to enlistment, as every candidate must satisfy all prescribed requirements before being admitted into the Service. He urged affected candidates who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints through the designated email address, helpdesk@customs.gov.ng, for consideration. Maiwada advised applicants to provide accurate information to facilitate the examination of their cases, adding that the initiative was designed to address genuine grievances without compromising the integrity of the recruitment process. Read also: Customs hands over N511m illicit drugs, codeine syrup to NDLEA, NAFDAC He reiterated that candidates who utilise the review window would undergo fresh screening, while cases involving established criminal conduct, including certificate fraud, would be referred to the appropriate authorities for legal action and prosecution. The Customs spokesman emphasised that the review should not be interpreted as a relaxation of recruitment standards or a guarantee of admission into the training college. He appealed to the affected applicants and the general public to remain calm and channel their complaints through the designated platform. Maiwada said the Service, under Adeniyi’s leadership, remained committed to a credible, transparent and accountable recruitment process. He added that Customs would not compromise the standards required of personnel responsible for national security, border protection, revenue collection and public safety. items.title: NGX Group named Africa’s best Exchange at Euromoney Markets Awards 2026
items.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa & Glory Bassey Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has been named Africa’s Best Exchange at the Euromoney Markets Awards 2026, recognising its contribution to market infrastructure, digital innovation and capital formation. Presented at the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, London, on Thursday, 15 October 2026, the award recognises achievements in market development during 2025 and comes amid robust growth in Nigeria’s equities market. A key driver of wider primary-market participation has been NGX Invest, the Group’s electronic public-offering platform, which simplifies subscriptions to public offers and rights issues. The platform played a significant role in Nigeria’s banking sector recapitalisation exercise, facilitating more than N2.8 trillion in capital raising. By September 2026, its distribution network had grown to more than 180 channels spanning stockbrokers, banks and fintechs, with a WhatsApp subscription channel providing investors with an additional channel for subscribing to public offers. Nigeria’s equities market recorded strong growth in 2025, with the NGX All-Share Index gaining 51.19 per cent, equities turnover rising 109.48 per cent to N5.96 trillion and market capitalisation reaching N99.38 trillion. This momentum has continued in 2026. As of 16 October, the All-Share Index had gained 59.07 per cent year-to-date. Equities turnover stood at N7.82 trillion, up 73.78 per cent from N4.50 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025, while market capitalisation reached N160.73 trillion. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “This award reflects our continued commitment to strengthening the infrastructure and technology that support capital formation and investment. ‘‘We appreciate the trust and collaboration of our regulators, policymakers, issuers, investors, the stockbroking community and other market participants, whose support contributes to the development of our capital market. ‘‘By widening digital access to investment opportunities, improving market efficiency and deepening connections with other African markets, we are working to make our capital market more accessible, resilient and competitive.” ‘‘We see this not simply as an achievement, but as encouragement to keep building a market that can mobilise capital for businesses and offer broader investment opportunities.” Beyond digital innovation, NGX Group continues to advance sustainable finance through the NGX Net-Zero Programme (N-Zero), implemented in partnership with DEG Impulse gGmbH and Africa Foresight Group, with support through DEG Impulse’s develoPPP programme. The initiative helps Nigerian businesses strengthen climate readiness, establish science-based emissions-reduction targets and develop transition plans that can support access to climate-aligned finance. items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Starting the 2027 Strategic Planning Process
items.description: By Ernest De-Graft Egyir Insight. Strategic planning for 2027 should begin before the current year closes. CEOs who wait until December risk making important decisions under time pressure, relying on incomplete analysis, or carrying existing priorities into the new year without sufficient review. Starting early gives the executive team time to examine current performance, understand market developments, reassess strategic assumptions, and determine what the organization must do differently to achieve its next set of objectives. Key Strategies: Review current-year financial and operational performance. Assess changes in customer expectations, competition, technology, and the broader business environment. Identify strategic assumptions that need to be reconsidered. Consult executives and relevant stakeholders on emerging priorities. Establish a realistic planning timetable with clear responsibilities and milestones. CEO Leadership Actions. Initiate the 2027 strategic planning process with the executive team. Require evidence-based assessments of current performance and future opportunities. Identify the major strategic questions that leadership must resolve before approving the 2027 plan. Actionable Tip. Ask your executive team: “What have we learned in 2026 that should fundamentally influence our strategy for 2027?” Why This Matters? Early planning creates room for better analysis, meaningful discussion, and deliberate resource allocation. It allows the CEO to enter 2027 with a clearer direction rather than spending the first quarter correcting decisions that should have been made earlier. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee

items.title: ‘APC has more problems within’ - Ndume affirms Shettima’s fear
items.description: Senator Ali Ndume, representing Borno South, has backed Vice President Kashim Shettima’s concern about internal divisions within the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the ruling party faces more problems within its ranks than from the opposition. Ndume said opposition parties might be resilient and vocal ahead of the 2027 general elections, but argued that the struggle for power and the focus on personalities rather than ideas were more troubling. “I think the Vice President was just blunt. We have more problems within than without because, seeing that the opposition, quite alright, they are both resilient, tough and talking big, but it’s not the major problem,” the senator said. He added that politicians across party lines largely shared similar backgrounds, arguing that their differences were often driven by political platforms and the struggle for power. “That’s why they talk about personality instead of ideas, instead of events or debates on what to do and how to do it, and that’s dangerous,” Ndume said. The lawmaker accused politicians of taking Nigerians for granted, urging greater attention to policy debates and practical solutions to the country’s challenges. Ndume’s remarks followed Shettima’s recent warning that internal divisions within the APC posed a greater concern to the ruling party than its political opponents. The Vice President spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the unveiling of the campaign head office of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a northern coalition supporting the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, where he also inaugurated the group’s campaign structure. “Honestly, I am not afraid of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household,” Shettima said. He maintained that unity within the ruling party would be crucial, adding, “If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer.” Shettima also warned northern political leaders against supporting Tinubu’s presidential campaign while undermining APC governors contesting at the state level. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said. He urged party members to support APC governors, National Assembly members and Tinubu ahead of the next round of elections. “Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” the Vice President added. items.title: Eko Power affirms status as Lagos state-licensed electricity distributor
items.description: By Jackson-Kalio Tokoni Eko Power Limited has affirmed its status as the electricity distribution company licensed by the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) to serve the southern parts of Lagos State. The company said its establishment followed changes to Nigeria’s electricity regulatory framework, which devolved regulatory powers over intrastate electricity generation, transmission and distribution to state governments. “Eko Power Limited is the distribution company licensed by the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) to distribute power in the southern parts of Lagos State,” the company said in a statement. It explained that the transition followed the Electricity Act 2023, as amended, and the 2023 constitutional amendment, which empowered state governments to regulate electricity markets within their jurisdictions. The transition was completed in June 2025, when LASERC assumed regulatory responsibility for retail electricity distribution and end-user tariffs in the state, the company added. Explaining its regulatory status, Eko Power said it operates under a distribution licence issued directly by LASERC and is subject to the commission’s tariff methodology and service-level standards. “This is reflected in Eko Power Limited’s own LASERC-approved cost-reflective tariffs and its published service-level commitments across all customer bands and feeders in Lagos State,” it said. “Eko Power Limited exists today because Lagos State exercised its constitutional right to regulate retail electricity distribution within the state,” the company said. “We are licensed by LASERC for distribution and tariffs, and our service commitments to customers are set independently under Lagos State law.” The post Eko Power affirms status as Lagos state-licensed electricity distributor appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Military air strikes neutralise 103 terrorists in North-East
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Joint Task Force (North-East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), has reported the neutralisation of 103 terrorists and the destruction of several logistics hubs and storage facilities in seven precision air strikes conducted across its area of operations between October 10 and 18, 2026. The military said the intelligence-led operations targeted Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters, their leadership structures and logistics networks in parts of Borno and Adamawa states. The OPHK spokesperson, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations involved coordinated deployments of Nigerian Army Aviation, the Nigerian Army Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (NARPAS) Regiment and Air Component assets. He said the operations were aimed at dismantling terrorist networks, disrupting their logistics and denying them freedom of action. According to Goni, the seven strikes targeted terrorist locations around Gudumbali in Guzamala Local Government Area (LGA) on October 10; Badu in Monguno LGA on October 11; Mairari in Guzamala and an area east of Badu on October 13; and Duste Uku in Gombi LGA of Adamawa State on October 16. Another operation was conducted on October 18 against the alternate residence of Abu Saleem, identified by the military as the ISWAP Wali of South Lake Chad, in the Arina Woje area of Monguno LGA, Borno State. Strike Targets ISWAP Leader’s Residence Goni said the October 18 operation followed intelligence gathering, surveillance and reconnaissance activities targeting Abu Saleem’s alternate residence. He said subsequent human intelligence confirmed the neutralisation of Jindullah, described as a prominent ISWAP fighter who reportedly served as Abu Saleem’s chief security guard. Read also: Troops kill scores of terrorists in Borno airstrikes The intelligence also confirmed the death of Abul Kissa, identified as a member of the group’s Shura Council, alongside other prominent fighters at the targeted premises. According to the spokesperson, the strike destroyed the structure and key logistics assets, including nine boat engines and several motorcycles stored there. He said the operation also disrupted the terrorists’ concealment arrangements in the forested area, further undermining their ability to use the location as a safe haven. Air Strike Hits Gathering of Over 100 Terrorists The military also reported a significant strike on October 13, when a Guardian air asset tracked a group of 16 terrorists from the Mairari axis to a gathering of more than 100 terrorists accompanied by several motorcycles. Goni said the gathering was located approximately 23 kilometres east of Badu and 19 kilometres west of Monguno LGA. He said a subsequent precision strike resulted in the assessed neutralisation of approximately 30 terrorists, although the extent of damage to the motorcycles could not be confirmed. The remaining operations targeted terrorist elements and facilities around Gudumbali, Badu, Mairari and Duste Uku. Goni said the seven strikes collectively resulted in the reported neutralisation of 103 terrorists and the destruction of several logistics hubs and storage facilities, significantly disrupting ISWAP’s operational capabilities and capacity to sustain its activities. He attributed the reported successes to intelligence-led operations and coordination among Nigerian Army Aviation, NARPAS, the Air Component and ground forces. The spokesperson said Operation Hadin Kai would sustain the operational momentum to degrade terrorist capabilities, disrupt command structures, deny insurgents safe havens and advance efforts to restore lasting peace and security across the North-East. items.title: Autonomous Shipping Regime: Experts warn against fire brigade approach
items.description: By Godwin Oritse Maritime experts have urged Nigeria’s maritime authorities to begin preparations ahead of the International Maritime Organisation’s (IMO) 2032 deadline for the implementation of the autonomous shipping regime, under which vessels will be operated remotely with minimal human intervention. The global autonomous shipping regime, structured under the IMO MASS Code (Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships Code), represents a historic shift in maritime law. Formally adopted as a voluntary framework at the 111th session of the Maritime Safety Committee (MSC 111), it is scheduled to become legally mandatory worldwide on January 1, 2032, under the SOLAS (Safety of Life at Sea) Convention. The regime aims to transition the industry from isolated national trials into a universally standardized, harmonized global framework Speaking at the 2026 Annual General Meeting of the Nigerian Association of Master Mariners (NAMM), a former Executive Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Captain Olugbemiga Abidoye, said port infrastructure alone was insufficient to achieve maritime excellence. He noted that Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) were already being developed and tested across the global shipping industry. The former ship captain warned that with just six years remaining before the 2032 deadline, Nigeria was lagging in preparations for autonomous shipping, noting that the country had yet to amend its maritime legislation to accommodate the transition to ports capable of receiving and supporting autonomous vessels. He stated: “Legislative amendments can take years, communication systems can take years to procure and integrate, while inter-agency procedures require consultation, training and testing. “The Code is goal-based; we must demonstrate safety outcomes, not just equipment purchases.” Similarly, a former General Manager, Marine and Operations, at the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Captain Ihenach Ebubeogu, said the government’s efforts to modernise ports across the country must bridge the gap between technological advancement and infrastructure upgrades. He stressed the need to integrate terminal digitalisation, robotic cargo-handling systems and workforce development to ensure seamless and efficient port operations. The post Autonomous Shipping Regime: Experts warn against fire brigade approach appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: IEAG demands probe into reported MSC office assault, warns of rising tensions at Tema Port
items.description: The Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) has called for an impartial investigation into a reported assault incident at the Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) office at the Tema Port, warning that unresolved operational challenges could trigger further confrontations between port users and service providers. The Association says persistent delays in shipping invoices, payment confirmation and container releases, alongside mounting charges and disruptions to cargo movement, are increasing financial pressure on businesses operating at the port. In a press statement dated October 19, 2026, IEAG’s Executive Secretary, Samson Asaki Awingobit, condemned violence and unlawful conduct while urging the authorities to investigate the reported incident and address the underlying grievances. “Any allegation of assault must be investigated impartially by the appropriate authorities, and anyone found culpable must be dealt with in accordance with the law,” the statement said. The Association cautioned that prolonged delays and uncertainty over essential shipping services could heighten frustration among importers, clearing agents and other port users, potentially leading to further confrontations. IEAG warned that unresolved tensions could result in serious injuries, property destruction, disruptions to port operations and threats to the safety of workers and the wider port community. “The authorities must not wait for a preventable confrontation to result in serious injury or loss of life before taking decisive action,” it said. Beyond the reported MSC office incident, the Association raised concerns about disruptions at the Meridian Port Services (MPS) Terminal 3, where more than 120 trucks reportedly scheduled to transfer containers were delayed by issues attributed to terminal operations. According to IEAG, such disruptions can prolong truck turnaround times, increase the cost of container movements, affect haulage schedules and create bottlenecks across the wider logistics chain. The Association said allegations that the delays were contributing to the accumulation of rent, storage and other charges had not been independently established and should be investigated transparently. It has called on the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), working with MPS and other relevant stakeholders, to establish the causes of the disruptions, determine responsibility and clarify the basis for any additional charges imposed on affected port users. IEAG is also urging the Minister for Finance to convene an emergency meeting involving the Ghana Shippers’ Authority, GPHA, shipping lines, terminal operators and other industry stakeholders to address the operational challenges and security concerns. The Association wants the meeting to secure enforceable service timelines, effective complaints mechanisms, transparent performance monitoring and fair treatment of additional charges where service-provider failures are established. It also wants applicable Service Level Agreements to be enforced, arguing that shipping lines and terminal operators must be held accountable for their obligations just as shippers are expected to comply with container-return deadlines and other contractual requirements. “Accountability in the maritime sector must be reciprocal. Shippers must fulfil their obligations, but shipping lines and terminal operators must equally be held accountable for the services they are contracted or required to provide,” the statement said. IEAG says a coordinated intervention is necessary to restore confidence, improve port efficiency and prevent further escalation of tensions within Ghana’s maritime trade and logistics sector.

items.title: IEAG urges Finance Minister to convene emergency meeting over Tema Port crisis
items.description: The Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) has called on the Minister for Finance to convene an emergency stakeholder meeting to address persistent shipping-line delays, terminal disruptions and mounting financial losses at the Tema Port. The Association says delays in invoicing, payment processing and container releases, coupled with reported disruptions at the Meridian Port Services (MPS) Terminal 3, are increasing costs for importers, exporters, freight forwarders, clearing agents and transport operators. In a press statement issued on October 19, 2026, and signed by its Executive Secretary, Samson Asaki Awingobit, IEAG warned that the challenges were undermining port efficiency, disrupting supply chains and heightening tensions within Ghana’s maritime trade sector. The Association is demanding an emergency, high-level meeting involving the Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA), Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), shipping lines, terminal operators and other relevant stakeholders to establish the causes of the delays, identify those responsible and agree on immediate relief measures. “The matter therefore requires urgent ministerial attention and coordinated intervention rather than routine stakeholder engagements that do not produce measurable results,” the statement said. IEAG is particularly concerned that delays in the issuance of invoices, payment confirmation and container releases can expose businesses to additional demurrage, rent, storage and related charges, even when they have fulfilled their payment and documentation requirements. The Association argues that businesses should not be made to bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. It has therefore urged the Finance Minister to secure firm commitments from shipping lines on invoicing timelines, payment processing, container release procedures and complaint resolution, as well as appropriate remedies where service failures are established. IEAG has also called on the GSA to investigate complaints and pursue appropriate measures within its statutory mandate, while urging the GPHA to strengthen oversight of port operations and work with terminal operators to address bottlenecks. The Association further wants applicable Service Level Agreements to be enforced through measurable performance standards, clear turnaround times, defined responsibilities and appropriate remedies for breaches. “The message is clear: Ghana’s port users cannot continue to absorb the financial consequences of persistent service delays while the underlying operational failures remain unresolved,” the statement said. IEAG insists that the proposed meeting must produce concrete decisions, deadlines and assigned responsibilities, with an effective mechanism for monitoring implementation. It says urgent intervention is necessary to restore operational efficiency, protect legitimate commercial interests and prevent further escalation of tensions at the Tema Port.

items.title: Kwakye Ofosu takes on Bawumia; accuses him of a U-turn on exchange rate stability
items.description: The Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has accused former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia of changing his position on the importance of exchange rate stability in assessing Ghana’s economic performance. Mr Kwakye Ofosu argues that Dr Bawumia, the New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer, previously placed considerable emphasis on the stability of the cedi but is now downplaying the indicator in his assessment of the economy under President John Dramani Mahama’s administration. The exchange follows Dr Bawumia’s recent criticism of the government’s economic management, in which he questioned whether improvements in inflation and the performance of the cedi had translated into meaningful relief for ordinary Ghanaians. The former Vice President has described the current situation as a “paper economy” and a “pocket economy”, arguing that improved macroeconomic indicators do not necessarily reflect the financial realities confronting households struggling with the cost of living. Speaking in an interview with Citi FM on Monday, October 19, Mr Kwakye Ofosu challenged Dr Bawumia to reconcile his current position with his previous public statements on exchange rate stability. “Today, Bawumia says that stability is not important. I can send you about three different clips of him prior to the 2024 elections in which he stoutly defended stability,” he said. He further questioned the former Vice President’s earlier emphasis on the exchange rate as a major measure of economic performance, asking: “Was he not the one who told us that the most important indicator in an economy like ours is the exchange rate? Was he not the one who told us this in 2014?” Mr Kwakye Ofosu also defended the Mahama administration’s economic record, insisting that the country’s key performance indicators had improved compared with the situation inherited from the previous government. He acknowledged, however, that more work remained to be done to improve economic conditions for Ghanaians. “The truth is that every single measure of economic performance today is better than he left it,” he said, adding that the government would continue working to improve the situation. “Of course, it can always get better. There is no dispute about that, and we will continue to work assiduously as a government to ensure that things get better than they are today,” he added.

items.title: Pakistan, Qatar agree to strengthen internal security cooperation
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, have agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in internal security, according to a statement issued by the Interior Ministry on Tuesday. The two met in Doha and held a detailed exchange of views on enhancing cooperation in internal security, the statement said. They also discussed the current regional situation and matters relating to peace and stability. “The meeting reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two interior ministries,” the statement said, adding that a decision was made to strengthen mutual cooperation and partnership in internal security. The meeting came a day after Naqvi addressed the 8th Global Security Forum in Doha, where he said Pakistan and Qatar had worked together to promote regional peace and stability. He recalled the Lake Lucerne Summit in Switzerland , organised by Pakistan and Qatar to facilitate US-Iran talks. Praising Qatar’s role in the peace efforts, Naqvi said the two countries’ aim was to “stop further conflict and to save innocent lives”. “In the diplomacy of our time, when others chose sides, Qatar chose to keep talking. Pakistan has seen this closely because we have worked beside you,” he said. Naqvi last met Al Thani on July 28 in Doha, where the two discussed security cooperation and ways to further strengthen bilateral relations in the security sector.

items.title: Is Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15 million suit a face-saving writ?
items.description: By Evans Mawunyo Tsikata In this country, we have turned defamation suits into face masks. You wear one when the political air gets polluted, not necessarily because you want justice, but because you want to look like you want justice. The story is simple. Sammy Gyamfi, a lawyer who knows that truth is a complete defence to defamation, looked into a camera, called the Minority Leader an extortionist, and dared him to go to court. It was bold, emphatic. Honourable Alexander Afenyo-Markin, also a senior lawyer and Minority Leader of Parliament, obliged. He filed a GH¢15 million suit. Multimedia was even joined. The republic waited. The NPP communicators sharpened their talking points. Then the High Court, on 14 th October, threw the whole thing out. Not because Sammy Gyamfi proved his allegation. Not because the court found Afenyo-Markin to be anything. But because the writ itself was incurably defective. No sufficient particulars of the defamatory publication on the writ, contrary to Order 57 Rule 2 of C.I. 47. The court said you cannot cure that kind of defect with arguments in paragraph 12 of a statement of claim. You cannot amend your way out of an objection that is already pending. For a GH¢15 million case, that is not a small mistake. That is like buying a brand new V8 to go to court and forgetting the engine at home. And that is why Ghanaians are laughing. Not in a happy way. In that painful, “ah, so this is what we have become” way. Let us be honest. The initial writ looked like face-saving. A national controversy erupts. Your name is dragged on every WhatsApp platform. Your own party communicators tell you privately that they are tired of defending you. The only way to show strength is to file. So you file a big GH¢15 million suit. The headline alone is meant to scare. But filing is not litigating. If you truly want to clear your name, you go back to court. You file properly. You endorse the writ with the exact words complained of. You plead the particulars like a lawyer, not like a political communicator writing a press release. You serve the person, you let the court hear you, and you let Ghanaians hear the evidence. Because here is the political reality Afenyo-Markin must face: at the Public Accounts Committee, Sammy Gyamfi appeared. Those who wanted to pin him down could not. His delivery, to use the words of many who watched, was on point. He answered. Whether you like him or not, he spoke with a confidence that right-thinking persons found convincing. And so the burden has shifted, not in law, but in public opinion. In law, the person who alleges must prove. In politics, the person whose name is mentioned must clear it. If Afenyo-Markin does not go back to court, properly, and make the process public, Ghanaians will believe Sammy Gyamfi. That is not law. That is how public trust works. You cannot file a defective writ, lose on a technicality, and then expect us to clap for you and move on. If Sammy Gyamfi has no evidence, let the court expose him. Let him be made to prove his emphatic claim to strict proof. But if he has the evidence he claims to have, then let it also come out. That is why the call from even NPP communicators themselves is instructive. One of them said on TV last week: “He needs to exonerate himself. If he doesn’t, he must be removed as Minority Leader. He should not even contest Effutu.” That is not an NDC person speaking. That is your own house telling you the kitchen is too hot. So, Hon. Afenyo-Markin, give us a break from incurably defective face-saving. Go back to court. File it right. Serve it right. Let us hear it in open court. Until then, forgive us if we listen to the man who sounded like he had evidence, over the man whose writ sounded like an apology letter that forgot its own address. Evans Mawunyo Tsikata

items.title: FCT police summon farmers, herders’ leaders over Dabiri, Paiko violence
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has summoned leaders of farmers and herders in Dabiri and Paiko villages, Gwagwalada Area Council, for a peace meeting following reports of violence threatening security in the communities. The Commissioner of Police, Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, met with representatives of both groups at the command headquarters in Abuja on Monday, October 19, 2026, as part of efforts to de-escalate tensions, restore public confidence and prevent further violence. The command’s spokesperson, SP Josephine Adeh, said Sanusi urged the farmers and herders to embrace dialogue, mutual understanding and peaceful coexistence, warning that disputes must be resolved through lawful means rather than violence. The police commissioner cautioned the leaders against incitement, retaliation and other actions capable of escalating tensions, stressing that violence would only endanger lives and undermine peace in the affected communities. He also urged both groups to cooperate with the police by identifying and handing over individuals allegedly responsible for the attacks. Read also: Police arrest four suspected cultists in Ogun According to him, the actions of a few individuals should not be allowed to threaten the safety of entire communities, making cooperation between residents and security agencies essential to restoring lasting peace. The command said the situation was under control and normalcy had been restored, adding that security measures had been strengthened to prevent a fresh breakdown of law and order. It urged residents of Dabiri, Paiko and neighbouring communities to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel deployed to the affected areas. The police also encouraged law-abiding residents to resume their legitimate activities without fear, while appealing to farmers and herders to maintain peaceful relations and avoid actions that could reignite hostilities. The command further urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station or through its emergency lines: 08032003913 and 08061581938.
